newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solvay to build German peroxide plant.
newsitem.headline: Solvay to build German peroxide plant.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drugs group Solvay SA said on Wednesday it would build an ultra high purity hydrogen peroxide plant in Germany to supply leading European semiconductor manufacturers.

The state of the art plant, to be built by Solvay's Interox hydrogen peroxide unit, will be in Bernburg and start up late in 1997. Other plants are in Munich in Germany, Warrington in England, and Deer Park in the U.S. state of Texas.
Ultra high purity hydrogen peroxide is used as a cleaning agent to remove organic materials, metallic impurities and particles during the microchip production process.

Solvay had no details on the cost of the plant with an annual capacity of some 5,000 tonnes of the high value added product. It already has a "classic" hydrogen peroxide plant in the area, near the city of Dresden in the former East Germany.
A Solvay spokesman said the location had been picked because it was near several major semiconductor producers. This would reduce the chances of the product becoming contaminated during transport.
Solvay's main European competitor for ultra high purity hydrogen peroxide is Merck of the U.S.
The spokesman said that the semiconductor manufacturers in the Dresden area were Siemens and IMD.
